text:
customer_ops: customer reported a sudden spike of 429s + intermittent 401s after migrating their ingress to an on-prem NLB. They claim traffic volume hasn't changed but our gateway shows quota exhaustion. Can we triage?

alex_m: do we have request headers/logs? specifically X-Forwarded-For and the remote_addr the gateway sees. also any recent k8s/ingress changes?

customer_ops: quick paste of relevant lines from their access logs (sanitized):
```
[2024-01-09T12:02:11Z] 10.32.4.5 GET /v1/generate 429 - "-" "curl/7.85" xff="-" auth="token:abc***"
[2024-01-09T12:02:12Z] 10.32.4.5 POST /v1/chat 401 - "-" "sdk/1.2" xff="-" auth="token:def***"
```
They also noted kube-proxy was upgraded and they switched to an NLB without proxy-protocol enabled around the same time.

priya: sounds like classic client-IP normalization issue — the ingress/GW is losing original client IP and seeing the same source (10.32.4.5) for many clients. our rate limiter is keyed by src IP by default for onprem gateway, so bursts from many users behind NAT will look like one big client and hit quota. 401s are likely separate (expired tokens) but the quorum 429s align with XFF missing.

hector: quick mitigation you can push to customer: 1) preserve client ip in ingress (enable proxy-protocol on NLB or use service annotations for the ingress controller) 2) change rate-limit key to be token/id-based until they roll out proxy-protocol. example k8s nginx annotation we suggested: `metadata.annotations: { "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol": "*" }`

priya: repro steps we gave them to validate locally:
1) curl from two different machines behind NAT -> both requests show same remote_addr at gateway.
2) enable proxy-protocol on NLB or set ingress controller to forward X-Forwarded-For.
3) re-run and confirm XFF populated.

hector: envoy local_rate_limit snippet we used in a canary to fallback to header-based key (only as a stopgap):
```
filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.local_rate_limit
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
    stat_prefix: http_local_rate_limiter
    token_bucket:
      max_tokens: 100
      tokens_per_fill: 100
      fill_interval: 1s
    filter_enabled:
      runtime_key: local_rate_limit_enabled
    response_headers_to_add:
    - header:
        key: x-local-rate-limit
        value: "true"
    descriptor_key: request.headers[\"x-api-key\"]  # prefer API key / token id as key when available
```
Note: descriptor_key is concept; match implementation to your proxy. we used header extraction to avoid IP-based collisions.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canaryed ingress change to preserve XFF on staging at 1707654380 (ingress-controller: nginx/1.3.2 -> applied annotation).

lisa_sre: long-term recommendations we gave ops & the customer: 1) make rate-limiter key pluggable — prefer user_id / api_key_id / jwt.sub rather than src IP for private gateways behind shared NAT. 2) implement token-level quotas and per-tenant leaky-bucket smoothing (e.g., window 1s, burst capacity tuned to workload). 3) for AWS NLBs, enable proxy protocol v2 and ensure ingress controller is configured to accept it, or use a target group with proxy support. 4) increase burst bucket temporarily (eg 20 -> 100) while they finish migration so clients don't hit false positives.

alex_m: customer-facing playbook we shared (short):
- check X-Forwarded-For in gateway access logs
- if missing, enable proxy-protocol on LB or configure ingress to forward XFF
- short-term: switch rate limit key to api-key or jwt-sub in gateway config
- rotate expired tokens for the 401s
- monitor p99 latency and 429 rate for 24h

customer_ops: customer enabled proxy protocol on their NLB and confirmed XFF is present upstream. they reported 0 429s in the first 2h after change, still clearing a few 401s from expired tokens which we advised on rotating. they'll monitor for 24h and ask us to reopen if anything else. thanks team :tada:
